classification.difficultyReason: Reduce both factors modulo 5 and interpret the product's remainder as a position in a repeating finger cycle.

content.prompt: Eric has a packet of 37 Smarties. He counts them out on his five fingers, over and over again, 19 times in fact. What finger does he end on? (Don’t calculate $37\times19$, use modulo arithmetic.)

answer.short:
The third finger in his counting order.

The total count has remainder $3$ modulo $5$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}37&\equiv2\pmod5\\19&\equiv4\pmod5\\37\times19&\equiv2\times4\pmod5\\37\times19&\equiv3\pmod5\end{align*}$$
Each complete cycle uses five fingers, so Eric ends on the third finger in his counting order.
